title: The filesystem tree
summary: One tree rooted at /, where things live, and how paths name them.

steps.title: One tree, rooted at /
body: Linux has no `C:` or `D:`. Everything, every disk, USB stick and network share, hangs off **one tree** whose top is `/` ("root").
├── home/ana       your files (~ is short for this)
├── tmp            scratch space, wiped on reboot
This layout is the **Filesystem Hierarchy Standard**. Knowing it means you can walk onto any server and guess where the config and the logs are.

items: Why the web server crashed last night
steps.explain: Config lives in `/etc`, things that grow live in `/var` (logs in `/var/log`), and people's files live in `/home`.

steps.title: Absolute and relative paths
body: - An **absolute** path starts with `/` and means the same thing from anywhere: `/var/log/syslog`.
- A **relative** path starts from where you are (the *current working directory*): `logs/app.log`.
- `.` is "here", `..` is "the parent", `~` is your home directory.
$ cd ../downloads     # up one, then into downloads
$ cd -                # back to the previous directory

steps.prompt: You are in `/home/ana/projects/api`. What does `pwd` print after these commands?
steps.explain: `../..` climbs to `/home/ana`, then into `downloads`. `./old/..` goes into `old` and straight back out.

steps.title: Looking around with ls
body: | `-l` | long format: permissions, owner, size, date |
| `-a` | all, including **dotfiles** (names starting with `.` are hidden) |
| `-t` | sort by modification time, newest first |
The first character of a long line is the type: `d` directory, `-` file, `l` symlink.

steps.prompt: Complete the command that lists everything, hidden files included, in long format with human sizes, **oldest first**.
steps.explain: `-t` sorts newest first; `-r` reverses that. Flags can be bundled: `ls -lahtr`.

steps.prompt: Match each command to what it does.
A script runs `cat config.yml` and fails with *No such file or directory*, but `ls /opt/app` shows `config.yml` is there. What is the most likely cause?
options: The script's working directory is not `/opt/app`; use an absolute path or `cd` first
steps.explain: Relative paths resolve from the *current working directory* of the process, which for cron jobs and services is often `/` or the user's home.

steps.title: Find your way around a real deploy folder
prompt: `~/srv/app` is a deploy folder like many teams use: every release in its own dated folder under `releases/`, and a
symlink `current` that points at the live one. Look around with `cd`, `pwd`, `ls -la` and `readlink`, then write
1. `current.txt`: the **real absolute path** that `~/srv/app/current` points to, with no symlink left in it.
2. `hidden.txt`: the names of the **hidden** files in the live release, one per line (just the names, like `.env`).
3. Create the folder `~/srv/app/shared/logs/nginx`, including the missing parents, in one command.

checks.name: current.txt is the real path of the live release
checks.fail: `~/answers/current.txt` should hold the full path, starting with `/home/learner`, with the symlink resolved. `realpath` (or `readlink -f`) prints exactly that.

checks.name: hidden.txt lists the hidden files of the live release
checks.cmd: diff <(sed 's#.*/##' ~/answers/hidden.txt 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^\.\{1,2\}$' | sort) <(cd ~/srv/app/current/ && ls -A | grep '^\.' | sort)
checks.fail: `~/answers/hidden.txt` should list every name in `~/srv/app/current` that starts with a dot. `ls -A` shows them (without `.` and `..`).

checks.name: the nginx log folder exists
checks.fail: `~/srv/app/shared/logs/nginx` is not there yet. `mkdir -p` creates the missing parents too.

hints: `ls -la ~/srv/app` shows `current -> releases/2031-03-12`: a **relative** symlink. `cd ~/srv/app/current && pwd -P` prints where you really are.
`mkdir -p ~/srv/app/shared/logs/nginx` makes every missing folder on the way.
explain: `pwd` shows the *logical* path (with the symlink), `pwd -P` and `realpath` the *physical* one. That difference
matters when a release is switched: a process that `cd`-ed into `current` keeps running in the **old** release
folder, because it holds the real directory, not the name. That is why deploy tools restart services after flipping

steps.title: Mission: the first day
prompt: Time to use it on a real server. The Linux mission **The first day** drops you on Byte & Biscuit's machine with clues instead of documentation.
Do its task **Gary's hidden Wi-Fi password** there: `cd`, `ls -la` (hidden files start with a dot) and `cat`. The lab checks your answer, and this step passes when it is done.
steps.explain: Hidden files are only hidden from a plain `ls`: `ls -a` shows everything whose name starts with a dot, which is where most configuration lives.
